claims.statement: For fixed selector F(T,p), independent-set states of a rooted ordinary tree admit an exact branch-product decomposition of ranks and w_F, with cross-branch dependence confined to selected leaves supported at the root; root-centered legal two-for-one switches couple exactly two occupied branch roots. This identifies a reduction route but does not establish weighted Hall feasibility or S(T,p)<=0.
claims.scope: Arbitrary finite ordinary tree and fixed selected-leaf set F; the decomposition is unconditional. The proposed universal deletion-plus-two-for-one weighted Hall theorem remains unresolved under the primary eligible lower-region hypotheses.
claims.reason: The rooted product and boundary-weight formulas follow directly from independence and the definition of w_F, and give an exact structural constraint on any cut compression. No selector-preserving uncrossing, capacitated injection, universal Hall proof, or eligible positive complete-sum counterexample is supplied.

limitations: The weighted Hall reduction remains open for arbitrary cuts; a branchwise product argument alone fails to account for root-supported tags and competing root-switch demands.
No primary aggregate proof or eligible positive-sum counterexample was obtained.
No exhaustive computation or external literature result was used; supplied bounded flows remain limited to their stated cases.
